title: Residential Electricity Supply Rate Change Notice Terms by Plan
content:
Two kinds of rate change can reach a Residential Electricity Supply agreement: a monthly variable rate change, and a regulatory pass-through on a fixed rate. The plan terms fix the minimum notice for each and whether a pass-through is permitted at all.

| Plan | Minimum notice, variable rate change (calendar days) | Regulatory pass-through permitted | Minimum notice, regulatory pass-through (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Beacon Ridge Monthly Variable | 10 | no | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Price Lock 6 | 10 | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Price Lock 12 | 10 | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Price Lock 24 | 10 | no | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Free Nights 12 | 10 | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Clean Wind 12 | 10 | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Clean Wind 24 | 10 | no | 30 |

**Notice periods.** The minimum notice is the number of calendar days between the notice date of the change and its effective date.

**Which cycles a new variable rate reaches.** On every plan, a new variable rate applies to the billing cycles that begin on or after its effective date; a cycle that began before the effective date keeps the earlier rate for the whole cycle.

**Pass-through permission.** A plan marked "yes" may have its fixed rate adjusted during the term to pass through a change in law or regulation. On a plan marked "no" (Beacon Ridge Monthly Variable, Beacon Ridge Price Lock 24 and Beacon Ridge Clean Wind 24) no such adjustment is permitted.

Example (hypothetical dates): a variable rate change effective on the 15th of a month reaches a cycle that begins on the 15th or later, but not a cycle that began on the 14th.
